text.p: - Slovenia's Finance Ministry agrees to increase car insurance bonuses for drivers under 25 years of age by 35 percent.
- Slovenia's conservative People's Party spent the most on its electoral campaign for the November general election.

- Prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek met representatives of the People's Party, Christian Democrats and the Desus party in an effort to form a broader coalition. Drnovsek must present a new government line-up after the previous one was rejected in parliament last week.
- Financially troubled newspaper Republika, which stopped publication last week, will be published weekly instead of daily.

- Slovenia's chances to join NATO increased significantly following NATO's invitation to Slovenia to join the Stabilisation Force (SFOR) in Bosnia this spring, Foreign Minister Davorin Kracun and Defence Minister Jelko Kacin said on Tuesday.

- SBI index tumbled over eight percent on Tuesday, following the central bank's decision to introduce special share trading accounts for foreign investors. The central bank's move was very strict and incomprehensible, the bourse's chief executive said.
- According to preliminary estimates, the market value of Slovenian companies dropped by about 20 percent after the sell-off of share prices on Tuesday.
- Slovenian health resort operator and mineral water producer Radenska will be listed on the Ljubljana bourse, although the date still needs to be determined.
